cards.front: How does unequal auxin make a shoot bend?
cards.back: Cells on the side with more **auxin** elongate faster, so the shoot bends towards the side that grows more slowly.
cards.hint: Compare how fast the cells on each side of the shoot grow.

cards.front: Why does a shoot bend towards light arriving from one side?
cards.back: **More auxin** collects on the shaded side, so cells there elongate faster and the shoot bends towards the light.
cards.hint: Think about which side of the shoot is shaded.

cards.front: Why does a shoot grown sideways bend upwards?
cards.back: **Auxin** collects on the lower side and stimulates elongation there, so the shoot bends upwards, away from gravity.
cards.hint: Think about which side of the shoot grows faster.

cards.front: Why does a root bend in the opposite direction to a shoot when unequal auxin is present?
cards.back: A concentration that stimulates shoot growth **inhibits** root growth, so the lower side of a root grows more slowly and the root bends downwards.
cards.hint: Compare how the same hormone affects shoots and roots.

cards.back: **Plant hormones** made mainly in growing tips. They move to other parts of the plant and affect cell growth.
A **directional growth response** to a stimulus such as light or gravity. Growth towards the stimulus is positive; growth away is negative.

cards.front: What does a tropism actually change in a plant?
cards.back: It changes the **direction of growth** of a plant part. A tropism does not move an existing part of the plant from place to place.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say that auxin pulls a shoot towards light?
cards.back: Auxin does not pull the shoot. **Faster growth** on the shaded side makes the shoot bend towards the light.
cards.hint: Focus on what the cells on the shaded side are doing.

cards.front: What is rooting powder and what does it contain?
cards.back: A product containing **auxins** that encourages roots to develop on plant cuttings.

cards.front: Why are auxins used as selective weedkillers?
cards.back: They disrupt growth in many **broad-leaved weeds** while grasses are largely unaffected.
cards.hint: Compare how broad-leaved weeds and grasses respond to the hormone.

cards.back: They can **end seed dormancy** and promote germination, and can also encourage flowering or increase fruit size in some plants.

cards.front: What is ethene and what does it control?
cards.back: A **gaseous plant hormone** that controls fruit ripening. Growers expose harvested fruit to it so it ripens when needed.
cards.hint: Think about how this hormone reaches the fruit.
